question: A training manager has split a course redesign into four pieces: rewriting the learning objectives, updating the slide deck, refreshing the exercises, and drafting the end-of-course quiz. Which observation should shape the order?
options: A) The quiz is what learners remember most clearly, so drafting it first would set the standard for the rest of the course.
B) The slide deck is the largest piece, so starting there gets the greatest share of the work out of the way early.
C) The objectives govern the other three pieces, so they are settled first while those three can then run in any order.
D) The exercises take the longest to review by others, so they should be finished ahead of the remaining three pieces.
correct_answers: C) The objectives govern the other three pieces, so they are settled first while those three can then run in any order.
explanations: Assessment written before the objectives ends up defining them by accident, so the course is shaped by whatever the quiz happened to test.
Size is a workload observation. Building slides before the objectives are agreed means rebuilding them when the objectives change.

Correct. Only one real dependency exists here: slides, exercises and quiz all serve the objectives. Once the objectives are fixed, the remaining three are independent of each other and their order is a matter of convenience.
Review time is a scheduling consideration, and exercises built against objectives that later change will need reworking anyway.
